domain.quantified: Every input satisfying the published TypeScript shapes and the guards in these equations; no fixture or finite sample restriction.
domain.arithmetic: Safe scaled integers and bigint intermediates only; units and decimal precision are exact and every overflow, sign, whole-count, required-axis, and mismatch guard remains part of the equation.
domain.data: Non-proxied plain records plus ordinary native Array, Map, Set, String, RegExp, JSON, Math, Number, BigInt, Object, and Error semantics, with the input graph immutable for the duration of a call.
domain.catalog: Only exact validated InventoryCatalog instances with unshadowed itemRevision and packagingRevision methods and unchanged private maps/retained arrays.
domain.mutation: Only fresh local arrays, maps, sets, and scalar locals are mutated; caller-owned values, catalog state, projections, and prototypes are read-only.

excluded: Proxies, accessors, subclasses, monkey-patched built-ins, custom collection/string lookalikes, and own-property method shadowing.
Concurrent mutation of inputs or catalog/projection state during a call.
Structurally injected catalog objects that were not produced by the validated InventoryCatalog constructor path.

laws.equation: Measured inputs parse exact finite decimals, preserve axis/unit identity, reject duplicate or invalid axes, and resolve packages only through one exact retained revision; package multiplication and amount sums use aligned scaled-integer arithmetic and exact equality, with every membership, positivity, configured-axis, and whole-count guard preserved.

Identities reject empty or padded text, normalize qualified dimensions by code-unit order with duplicate rejection, and serialize fixed typed tuples; trace nodes enforce the lot-only item qualifier before serialization.

Intent arrays reject undefined and non-finite numbers recursively before JSON serialization; metadata recursively emits key-sorted, delimiter-safe JSON fragments, rejects undefined and non-finite values, and preserves array order.

Selectors validate the item, sort/deduplicate every allowed identity set, reject empty/ambiguous constraints and duplicate qualified dimensions, then match or compare subsets independently for every fixed and qualified dimension with omitted constraints remaining broad.
Use-by is the lexicographically earlier defined value from the exact lot and container identities; expiry is inclusive and false when neither value exists.

All supporting quantity and measurement helpers retain exact safe scaled-integer arithmetic, unit/precision guards, axis normalization, deterministic ordering, and fail-closed overflow or invalid-input behavior used by the amount laws.
